name: Miller Creek - Lewis and Clark SRA
note: Miller Creek area of Lewis and Clark SRA, the westernmost of its south-shore areas, on its own gravel spur about 2.4 km west of Bloomfield: Basic camping on grass and in tree-lined pull-offs along the boat-ramp road beside the Miller Creek inlet, with no marked pads; vault toilet, drinking water and a hiking trail. Pad size is unclear: a 2021 Dyrt reviewer advised a small rig or tent (the dirt road in from the west is rough and turns to mud after rain) and a 2026 Google reviewer called it tent-only, though Game and Parks lists it as Basic camping and 2022 imagery shows a trailer and truck in one of the pull-offs. Self-register at the Iron Ranger (cash or check). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: NGPC State Parks Guide 2026 p.62 (digital.outdoornebraska.gov/i/1545147/61, read 2026-11-05): 'Miller Creek - boat ramps, Basic camping, primitive restrooms and a hiking trail' + NGPC Lewis and Clark brochure map (outdoornebraska.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Lewis-Clark-Brochure-map-11-22-23.pdf via Wayback 2026-08-18): Miller Creek Area with a non-reservable camping icon, restroom, drinking water, boat ramp and trailhead, on its own spur off R54C + NGPC park page (Wayback 2026-08-18): all camping outside Weigand/Burbach is first-come, first-served by Iron Ranger + Esri Wayback 2022-06-25 at 42.82904,-97.66270: a ~10 m trailer-sized white unit and a pickup parked in a pull-off under the trees beside the ramp road -> real NGPC drive-in basic campground (pad size unclear: kept with a caveat per the 2026-11-02 rule; Dyrt 2021 'small rig or tent' is the vague tier; the only 'tent only' statement is a 2026 bikepacker's Google review, not the agency's). Public: no price gate. Google Maps 'Miller Creek Campground - Lewis and Clark SRA' at 42.83000,-97.66229, phone 402-388-4169, 4.4 on 12 reviews, open. Separate place: 2.4 km W of Bloomfield 2673 on its own spur road; not on ReserveAmerica (park 230101 loops are all Weigand-Burbach).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-05: Esri World Imagery (2024-07-11, rendered) and Esri Wayback 2019-09-21 / 2022-06-25 (rendered) at 42.82905,-97.66270: the camping is in grass pull-offs on the WEST side of the gravel boat-ramp road; the Miller Creek inlet (a ~50 m backwater arm of Lewis and Clark Lake) lies 40-60 m east, across the road and a shrub/tree strip on the creek bank, and the open lake is ~300 m north past the ramp lot and a mowed field. Road between -> no on-water value; no confirmed open sightline from a site across the vegetated bank -> not waterfront (unsure goes down). No per-site map or ReserveAmerica record exists (not reservable). Dam check: Gavins Point Dam is ~25 km east; this is the lake side, DEM 383 m at the site vs ~367 m on the inlet water (above pool, not below a dam). The Google pin (42.83000,-97.66229) sits in the mowed field north of the ramp lot; no camping is visible there on any capture.

fees.note: Basic camping $15 a night in season, $10 mid-October through April. Plus tax and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year). Nebraska Game and Parks' camping rates grid ('These rates are consistent across all parks'). Not reservable, so no reservation fee.

fees_source: https://outdoornebraska.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2025-Camping-Rates-Grid.pdf (statewide Basic $15, $5 less mid-Oct to April) as already carried by sibling 2673 Bloomfield; the only class here is Basic (NGPC State Parks Guide 2026 p.62); entry permit amounts as in 2673's fees note, read 2026-11-05
booking_source: nebraskastateparks.reserveamerica.com campgroundDetails parkId 230101 read 2026-11-05: loops are Boat Dock, Burbach Cabins, Burbach Campground, Weigand Modern Campground, Weigand Shelter, Weigand Tent Camping Area (no Miller Creek); NGPC park page (Wayback 2026-08-18): 'Camping reservations are available for 75% of the campsites in Weigand and Burbach campgrounds ... All other camping is all first-come, first-served; campers must register their nightly camping fees in a raised, locked box called an Iron Ranger ... cash or checks only.'
flags: Pad size / RV fit is the open question and is carried as a note caveat (rule of 2026-11-02): NGPC says 'Basic camping' (the 2026 guide says Bloomfield has 'Electric and Basic camping pads' but says only 'Basic camping' for Miller Creek); the brochure icon is 'Non Reservable Tent Camping', but NGPC uses the same icon at Bloomfield, where its own photo caption shows an RV; Google review by a bikepacker ~mid-2026: 'Primitive Camping/Tent only.'; Dyrt review 2021-08-30: 'you need to have a small rig or tent' (tied to the rough dirt road from the west); Esri Wayback 2022-06-25 shows a ~10 m white trailer-sized unit plus pickup in a pull-off at 42.82904,-97.66270 (empty grass pull-off with a worn track in 2019). If AWH reads the 2026 'tent only' review as decisive, this becomes a skip (tent-only).
Not on RV Life (Algolia bbox 42.80-42.86, -97.72 - -97.60 returns only Bloomfield), so no rating.

Pin is the pull-off where the 2022 imagery shows a trailer, ~25 m from The Dyrt's pin (42.82919,-97.66247); the Google pin (42.83000,-97.66229) is ~100 m north in the mowed field past the ramp lot. Site count unknown (a Google reviewer: 'lots of sites').
Access: from Crofton via NE-121 and Spur 54C (R54C), the same road as Bloomfield; the Dyrt reviewer warns the road west toward Hwy 12 is dirt, rough and muddy after rain.

Structured data for stamping: hookups.electric 0 (NGPC State Parks Guide 2026 p.62 lists only 'Basic camping'; brochure legend 'BASIC - NO ELECTRICAL SERVICE', read 2026-11-05); booking reservable false, fcfs always, platform operator (ReserveAmerica park 230101 has no Miller Creek loop; NGPC page: all camping outside Weigand/Burbach FCFS via Iron Ranger, cash or check); facilities: vault_toilets true ('primitive restrooms', NGPC guide 2026 + brochure restroom icon), potable_water true (brochure drinking-water icon at Miller Creek, 2023 map), boat ramp + trailhead (brochure); showers/dump not here (brochure shows them only at Weigand-Burbach); season not confirmed for this area (NGPC says camping is year-round SRA-wide but gives no Miller Creek specifics), so not stamped.
Fees: one class only (Basic), so no electric surcharge copied from 2673.
